content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices simultaneously? This encrypted messaging service now makes it easier for users to use the app across platforms between iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, no longer limited to using only an iPad as a secondary mobile device.

The company also announced Android linking support today, stating: "We are expanding the linked devices feature on iOS, allowing you to link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue."

When linking another iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their complete message history and media files stored within the past 45 days.

Signal stated that the transfer process uses the same "link-and-sync" technology as iPad and desktop devices (including Signal for Mac), with end-to-end encryption used throughout.

This expanded feature is particularly useful for users who need to keep work and personal iPhones separate, and is also suitable for those who need to test multiple devices.

This change also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, enabling seamless conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is now available on the App Store. Signal has previously also introduced a username feature, allowing users to contact each other without sharing phone numbers.
